chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibrahim ibn 'Umar al-Yamani, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, who said:
Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام) said: “O Jabir, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created the creation in three categories, and this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:”

“And you shall be three kinds. Then the companions of the right hand—what are the companions of the right hand? And the companions of the left hand—what are the companions of the left hand? And the foremost, the foremost—those are the ones brought near.”

So the foremost are the Messengers of Allah (عليهم السلام) and the specially chosen ones of Allah from His creation. He placed within them five spirits: He supported them with the Holy Spirit, by which they knew things; He supported them with the spirit of iman, by which they feared Allah, Mighty and Majestic; He supported them with the spirit of strength, by which they were able to obey Allah; He supported them with the spirit of desire, by which they desired obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and disliked disobedience to Him; and He placed within them the spirit of movement, by which people go and come.

And He placed in the believers and the companions of the right hand the spirit of iman, by which they feared Allah; and He placed in them the spirit of strength, by which they were able to obey Allah; and He placed in them the spirit of desire, by which they desired obedience to Allah; and He placed in them the spirit of movement, by which people go and come.

key_terms.أَزْوَاجًا ثَلَاثَةً: three categories or classes of creation
key_terms.السَّابِقُونَ: the foremost ones, identified here as the Messengers and Allah’s specially chosen servants
key_terms.الْمُقَرَّبُونَ: those brought near to Allah in rank and proximity
key_terms.رُوحَ الْمَدْرَجِ: the spirit connected to worldly movement and bodily going and coming
key_terms.رُوحِ الشَّهْوَةِ: the spirit of desire by which one desires obedience and dislikes disobedience
key_terms.رُوحِ الْإِيمَانِ: the spirit of faith by which one fears Allah
key_terms.رُوحِ الْقُدُسِ: the Holy Spirit by which the chosen ones know realities and things
key_terms.رُوحِ الْقُوَّةِ: the spirit of strength by which one is enabled to obey Allah

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) explain the three categories of people and the five spirits given to the prophets?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur’anic division of humanity into three categories and identifies the foremost ones as the Messengers of Allah (عليهم السلام) and His specially chosen servants. It describes the distinct spiritual endowments placed within them, especially the Holy Spirit, and contrasts these with the spirits granted to the believers among the companions of the right hand.
